summary: Changing --error-format to JSON replays cached human diagnostics.
scenario: Cold cache an rlib with an unused-variable warning using --error-format=human; delete outputs and request --error-format=json. Kache returns success and human stderr from a local hit while direct rustc emits JSON.
evidence: src/args.rs
Diagnostic format, JSON notification, color and width flags are excluded from parsed key inputs.
src/args.rs
Both separated and attached diagnostic-format flags are skipped before residual key arguments.
src/wrapper.rs
Hit diagnostics write saved stdout/stderr verbatim.
src/wrapper/hit.rs
A successful cache restoration reports the hit and replays the cached diagnostics.
trace: CLI rustc dispatch → RustcArgs skips diagnostic flags → key unchanged → restore hit → replay cached stderr verbatim → JSON consumer receives human text.
severity: Reached by changing valid diagnostic formatting on warning-producing Rust builds. Artifact bytes may be valid, but Cargo/IDE/custom JSON diagnostic consumers receive the wrong protocol. Both wrapped calls and the direct control succeeded; compiler_runs dropped from 1 to 0. Color/width/notification variants were source-reviewed, not independently proved.

message: CACHE_EMIT_DESTINATION: hit failed to materialize requested --emit=metadata path
summary: A rustc hit for an explicit emit destination restores the producer filename and omits the requested output.
scenario: Cold cache --emit=metadata=out/first.rmeta with JSON artifact notifications; remove outputs and request out/second.rmeta. The hit exits 0 and restores only first.rmeta; direct rustc creates second.rmeta.
evidence: src/args.rs
Emit kinds are retained, but only dep-info gets its explicit output destination retained.
src/wrapper.rs
Restore uses cached filename under output_dir unless the name matches explicit -o.
src/wrapper.rs
Each cached output is materialized using artifact_target_path.
trace: CLI RustcArgs parses --emit → metadata destination omitted → key unchanged → hit qualifies by metadata kind → cached first.rmeta restored under its old name → requested second.rmeta absent despite success.
severity: Direct rustc/custom build systems using explicit per-emit filenames receive a successful compiler result with the promised metadata artifact missing. Downstream consumers can fail or consume a stale pre-existing second file. Only metadata was executed; other explicit emission kinds need their own controls.

message: RUSTDOC_STALE_INPUT_nested: warm cache returned docs predating changed compiler input
summary: Rustdoc cache keys omit nested module files below a non-mod.rs module.
scenario: Eligible per-crate rustdoc invocation documents lib.rs → foo.rs → foo/child.rs. Cold child docs say OLD_MARKER. Edit only child.rs to NEW_MARKER and remove outputs. Kache hits the unchanged key and restores OLD_MARKER; direct rustdoc emits NEW_MARKER.
evidence: src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
The key hashes only paths returned by source_records.
src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Each module child resolves against the current file parent, losing the implicit foo/ directory of foo.rs.
src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Missing candidate child.rs/child/mod.rs paths are skipped.
src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Reusable entries restore and return successful local hits without running rustdoc.
trace: Rustdoc dispatch → cached --merge=none crate mode → source_records(foo.rs) resolves child at crate root → foo/child.rs omitted → unchanged key after real input edit → hit returns stale HTML.
severity: Routine Rust module layout in an enabled compatible rustdoc caching workload produces silently outdated API documentation after a source edit. Confirmed with installed rustdoc1.98.1 and 1.99 direct cached-mode invocations. Ordinary cargo doc and Cargo1.99 new meta flags pass through and are outside this trigger.

message: RUSTDOC_STALE_INPUT_outer_doc_include: warm cache returned docs predating changed compiler input
summary: Rustdoc cache keys omit files included by an outer documentation attribute.
scenario: lib.rs has #[doc = include_str!("README.md")] on a public function. Cold README contains OLD_MARKER; edit README to NEW_MARKER, delete output/parts, and rerun the same eligible rustdoc command. Kache restores OLD_MARKER; direct rustdoc emits NEW_MARKER.
evidence: src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Only scanner-selected source records enter the content key.
src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Outer attributes are skipped as a whole after optional path-attribute handling, so include_str! inside #[doc=...] is not visited.
src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Same-key cache hits restore the archive and return success.
trace: Rustdoc cached crate mode → scan_rust skips outer #[doc=include_str!(...)] → included README absent from source_records → README edit does not re-key → old docs restored.
severity: External documentation files on public items are routine valid Rust inputs. In supported caching mode, changing their text gives a successful hit with obsolete documentation. Inner #![doc=include_str!(...)] invalidates correctly in the separate green control; this outer-attribute finding is distinct from nested-module resolution.

message: RUSTDOC_STALE_INPUT_env: warm cache returned docs predating changed compiler input
summary: Rustdoc cache keys omit environment dependencies read by env! in documentation.
scenario: lib.rs has #![doc = env!("DOC_TEXT")]. Cold DOC_TEXT=OLD_MARKER; remove output/parts and rerun with DOC_TEXT=NEW_MARKER. With no custom key_env_vars declaration, Kache hits the identical key and restores OLD_MARKER; direct rustdoc emits NEW_MARKER.
evidence: src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Base key hashes selected files/options/externs/html inputs without compiler-reported env dependencies.
src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Environment folding uses only explicitly configured key_env_vars.
src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Source discovery explicitly does not read compiler dep-info.
src/compiler/rustdoc.rs
Public run passes config.key_env_vars and no discovered build/extra input digest.
trace: Rustdoc cached crate mode → file scanner sees unchanged source → only configured env names folded → DOC_TEXT value absent from key → same-key hit restores outdated HTML.
severity: Documentation derived from build environment, version strings or release labels can be wrong while all compiler calls succeed. Real env! expansion is proved on1.98.1 and 1.99. Manually configuring key_env_vars may work around a known variable, but automatic env dependency completeness is absent; unrelated proc-macro hidden inputs are not claimed.
